title: AI is Hollowing Out Tech Sector Jobs: Oracle and Microsoft Help Push Layoff Rate to 20-Year High
excerpt: Tech giants are pouring hundreds of billions into AI while quietly gutting the workforces that built them, and the labor data reveals a layoff rate that dwar...
content_html:
Rich Duprey

Quick Read

  • Tech's layoff rate hit 2.3% in June, surpassing peaks from the 2008 financial crisis and 2001 recession, as 63,000 workers were cut.

  • Oracle cut 21,000 jobs, representing 13% of its workforce, explicitly citing AI deployment, while Cisco and Intuit redirected labor savings into AI infrastructure.

  • AI accounts for 23% of all 2026 U.S. job cut announcements, though some companies may use the label to dress up ordinary cost-cutting.

  • Act now: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and Microsoft didn't make the cut. Grab the names FREE today.

The AI boom has created a strange split-screen economy. Companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on chips, data centers, and software while simultaneously shrinking the workforces that once powered the technology industry. The promised payoff is higher productivity, but the immediate result is becoming harder to ignore: fewer people are needed to produce more.

That tension is showing up in the labor data. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), the information sector's layoff rate jumped 0.7 percentage point in June to 2.3% -- meaning roughly 2.3% of workers were laid off or discharged during the month. The rate has more than doubled since November, as 63,000 workers were let go in June, the third-highest monthly total since April 2020.

Tech Layoffs Are Accelerating

The six-month moving average layoff rate climbed to 2.0%, its second-highest reading on record. For perspective, it peaked at roughly 1.5% during both the 2008 financial crisis and the 2001 recession.

This isn't simply an economic downturn story. The biggest technology companies are actively reshaping their labor needs around AI.

Oracle's 21,000-job reduction represented about 13% of its workforce and fully one-third of the quarter's total. Microsoft eliminated roughly 4,800 positions, or 2.1% of its global workforce, according to the company's July announcement.

The percentages become even more striking at smaller companies. Groupon (NASDAQ:GRPN) is cutting up to 400 positions, nearly 25% of its workforce, while ClickUp eliminated 22% of its staff and Intuit cut 17%.

快速阅读

  • 6 月份科技行业的裁员率达到 2.3%，超过了 2008 年金融危机和 2001 年经济衰退期间的峰值，裁员 63,000 人。
  • 甲骨文（Oracle）裁员 21,000 人，占其员工总数的 13%，明确提到人工智能部署，而思科和 Intuit 将节省的劳动力重新投入人工智能基础设施。
  • 人工智能占 2026 年美国所有裁员公告的 23%，尽管一些公司可能会用这个标签来粉饰普通的成本削减。
  • 立即行动：2010 年给 NVIDIA 打电话的分析师刚刚列出了他心目中的十大人工智能股票，而微软并未上榜。 今天免费获取名字。

人工智能的繁荣创造了一种奇怪的分屏经济。 公司在芯片、数据中心和软件上花费了数千亿美元，同时缩减了曾经为科技行业提供动力的劳动力。 承诺的回报是更高的生产率，但直接的结果变得越来越难以忽视：需要更少的人来生产更多的产品。

这种紧张局势体现在劳动力数据中。 根据美国劳工统计局的职位空缺和劳动力流动率调查 (JOLTS)，6 月份信息行业的裁员率上升了 0.7 个百分点，达到 2.3%，这意味着当月约有 2.3% 的工人被解雇或解雇。 自 11 月以来，这一比例增加了一倍多，6 月份有 63,000 名工人被解雇，这是自 2020 年 4 月以来的第三高月度总数。

科技公司裁员正在加速

六个月移动平均裁员率攀升至 2.0%，为有记录以来第二高。 从长远来看，它在 2008 年金融危机和 2001 年经济衰退期间都达到了约 1.5% 的峰值。

这不仅仅是一个经济衰退的故事。 最大的科技公司正在围绕人工智能积极重塑劳动力需求。

甲骨文裁员 21,000 人，约占其员工总数的 13%，占本季度总数的三分之一。 根据该公司 7 月份的公告，微软裁减了约 4,800 个职位，占其全球员工总数的 2.1%。

对于规模较小的公司来说，这一比例更为惊人。 Groupon（纳斯达克股票代码：GRPN）将裁员多达 400 个职位，占其员工总数的近 25%，ClickUp 则裁员 22%，Intuit 则裁员 17%。
